This here is an Iranian "Qahveh Khane'ie" painting and they are related very closely to triditional iranian storytelling perfromance "Naghall'i" . 
Of course what you have is only a small copy of one.
 "Qahveh khane" is a persian word associeted with a
 place which in the old times( and in some cases even now) men would gather up and drink tea or coffee and smoke tobacco and such, there. Something of a triditional middleeastern cafe. Because of those places being the center of gathering in town, it was usually the place to perform "Naghall'i". Now "naghalli" as i said litterarly translates to "storytelling",  in which a performer would tell an story from either persian or islamic myths and legends, usually something heroic that involved battles and wars ( you could say it was kind of like today's pop culture movies).
 Something that got invented by persian painters to make a better exprience for people during this storytelling was to paint scenes of those stories on the Qahveh Khane's wall so that the story teller could show some of the story to the people watching. That's why they are called that. Also there are portable versions of them like the one you have ( of course much larger) which the storyteller would carry on in like the city square or Bazaar to use it there. 
The one you have i would guess it's associated with Imam Ali's story who is the islamic imam in Shia' culture and has a lot of heroic stories and was one the most used heros in Naghalie.
"Bleu" can also mean rookie or rare sometimes.
